 Town Clerk 
 The Town Clerk’s Office serves as the central information point for local residents, citizens at large, departments, boards and committees.  The Town Clerk is the keeper of town records, the chief election official, a member of the Board of Registrars, Registrar for all vital birth, death, and marriage events occurring within the community and those events occurring elsewhere to local residents, serves as Burial Agent, serves as Super Records Access Officer and is the official keeper of the Town Seal.   Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed town officials.  Purchases, maintains, tests and secures all voting equipment.  Schedules, trains and supervises all election workers and voting precincts in accordance with state and federal regulations.  
   
 The Clerk's office maintains the local census and voter registration database, assists with verification of the Federal Census, maintains multiple data bases and issues various licenses and permits such as dog licenses, raffle permits, business certificates, underground and above ground flammable storage registrations, records and maintains Town Meeting votes pertaining to local acceptances of Mass. General Laws, Special Acts, general and zoning bylaws.  Records oaths of office, open meeting and conflict of interest law receipts for local officials.   Preserves permanent records such as births, marriages, deaths, marriage intentions, meeting minutes, planning and zoning board decisions and issues certified copies of these records upon request.  
   
 The Clerk's office works mainly under the direction of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, Attorney General Office's, Department of Revenue, in accordance with Federal Laws and Regulations, the Massachusetts General Laws, Special Acts, local Bylaws, rules and regulations, Selectmen and citizens of the Town of Barre. 
   
 REGULAR OFFICE HOURS   
 The office is open to the public Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m. 
 Appointments are also available outside of regular office hours. 
   
 Interested in being appointed as an Election Worker????   Contact the Town Clerk for more information or to apply!

 2026 Election Information 
 For more information on upcoming 2026 elections or town meeting click  here.

 Questions pertaining to Elections, Nomination Papers or Voter Registration/Status can be directed to the Town Clerk by calling 978-355-2504 ext 5.  or emailing   clerk@townofbarre.com 
    We respectfully ask that observers register 48 hours in advance by emailing  clerk@townofbarre.com  or calling the office at (978) 355-2504 ext 5.  Masks are optional. Interested in becoming an Election Worker?  Contact the Town Clerk for more information! 
   
 CAMPAIGN & FINANCE   
 
 
 Chapter 55 of Mass General Law governs the financing of political campaigns in Massachusetts. The statue requires that candidates and political committees disclose all contributions received and expenditures made. There are various limitations and prohibitions on certain sources of campaign contributions. Additionally, the manner in which campaign funds may be spent is regulated by this statue along with guidelines established by the  Office of Campaign and Political Finance . Chapter 28 of the Acts of 2009 made changes to the Campaign Finance Law requiring City and Town Clerks to post Campaign Finance Reports for candidates and ballot question committees when there has been $1,000 or more in activity.  These reports, and reports for political campaigns with under $1,000 in activity, are filed in the Town Clerk's office and are available to the public. Statement of Organization   (M101) 
 
 Any public employee who runs for elective office and will raise funds must have a committee organized on their behalf 
 MGL Chapter 55, section 13 prohibits paid state, county, city or town employees, from political fundraising, even for their own campaign  
 
 8th day Preceding Election Reports Must be Filed by: 
 
 All candidates/treasurers appearing on ballot 
 Treasurers for ballot question committees 
 
 Year end reports must be filed by: 
 
 
 
 All incumbents 
 All candidates/treasurers whose name appeared on ballot regardless of outcome 
 Treasurers of active ballot question committees 
 Treasurers of all other active candidate committees 
 
 
 
 
     
 
 
 
 
 What is Required for Filing with the Town Clerk?   
 
 M 102   is required for all candidates who HAVE received contributions, made expenditures (includes those who have spent their own money); or incurred obligations during the reporting period, or DO have a campaign fund in existence (balance).  
 Receipts of $50 or more must be itemized alphabetically on  Schedule A ; Candidates required to file an M 102 should disclose   the disposition of assets as receipts on Schedule A 
 Expenditures of $50 or more must be itemized alphabetically on   Schedule B 
 Any donations made of value (other than money) of $50 or more must be itemized on   Schedule C 
 Schedule D  is a cumulative schedule of ALL debts as of the last day of the reporting period 
 Click   here  for detailed information 
 M102-0   for candidates who HAVE NOT received contributions, made expenditures, or incurred obligations during the reporting period and DO NOT have a campaign fund in existence (balance). 
 
 The 30th day after election report is  no longer required   for communities who have adopted a city form of government with elections in November. Dissolution of Committee : Treasurers are required to retain a detailed account of receipts for 6 years from the date of the relevant election.

 ELECTIONS 
  ELECTION FILING DEADLINES LISTED BELOW - PLEASE TAKE NOTICE:
 
The Town Clerk’s Office is located at
40 West St., Basement and is generally open from 9am to 5pm on most Election Deadline dates unless otherwise posted.  
  TO DROP OFF  NOMINATION PAPERS OR PETITIONS  

 1.  Call  the office 978-355-2504 Ext 5 and/or email  clerk@townofbarre.com  to arrange for a time to drop off the Nomination papers in person. 
  OR       
  2.  Mail  (certified overnight/return receipt recommended)  - Mail nomination papers only if the deadline is not approaching  (regular mail allow at least 10 business days)  to: 

                        Ellen M. Glidden, CMC, CMMC, Barre Town Clerk 
                        ATTN:  NOMINATION PAPERS (OR PETITIONS) 
                        PO BOX 418 
                        Barre, MA 01005-0418 

 Include a pre-stamped and pre-addressed envelope so we can return a receipt for papers back to you.  We advise candidates to use some sort of tracking service if they are mailing their papers so they can ensure timely delivery. 
 Be sure to also call 978-355-2504 ext 5 and/or email   clerk@townofbarre.com   stating you have mailed your papers back. 

 3.  Drop Box   - Utilize the Large Blue Secure Ballot drop, locked box located to the right of the outdoor stairs.   Be sure to call 978-355-2504 ext 5 and/or email  clerk@townofbarre.com  BEFORE LEAVING nomination or petition papers in the box.     
  Please be sure to put them in an envelope with your contact information including your name, phone number, e-mail address and mailing address and clearly mark ATTENTION TOWN CLERK - TIME SENSATIVE - NOMINATION PAPERS ENCLOSED.    A receipt will be sent to you. 
   
 WHERE DO I GO TO VOTE? - THE TOWN OF BARRE HAS TWO POLLING LOCATIONS (PRECINCTS) 
  PRECINCT 1 VOTERS WILL VOTE AT THE SENIOR CENTER - 557 SOUTH BARRE ROAD 
 PRECINCT 2 VOTERS WILL VOTE AT AMERICAN LEGION POST 2 - 450 SOUTH BARRE ROAD 
 TO FIND OUT WHICH PRECINCT YOU ARE REGISTERED TO VOTE AT GO TO:   https://www.sec.state.ma.us/VoterRegistrationSearch/MyVoterRegStatus.aspx 
 OR call the Town Clerk's Office at 978-355-2504 EXT 5 
   
 VOTER REGISTRATION 
 The Deadline to Register to voter is 10 days prior to an election day   at 5pm  
 The Town Clerk's office will be open from 9am to 5pm on the last day to register. 
   For online voter registration, go to:  https://www.sec.state.ma.us/ovr/ 
 OR call the Town Clerk's Office at 978-355-2504 EXT 5 for further information. 
   
 CLICK HERE TO REGISTER TO VOTE, CHANGE YOUR NAME, CHANGE YOUR ADDRESS OR CHECK YOUR REGISTRATION INFORMATION 
    
 VOTING OPTIONS: 
 1.  In person on election day at the polling locations 
 2.  Absentee Voting (must qualify)   Absentee Ballot Application   
        The last day and time to vote in person by Absentee Ballot 12 noon business day before election.. 
 3.  Vote By Mail (must submit  application  to receive a ballot) 
        Deadline to apply for a Vote By Mail Ballot is by 5pm the 5th business day prior to election day. 
 4.  Accessible Voting  Voters with Disabilities            accessible application 
 5.  Military or Overseas Voters  Military and Overseas Voters   
                                                   Federal Post Card Application 
   
 ABSENTEE BALLOTS  
 To qualify for an   absentee ballot , you must: 
 
 Be away from your city/town on Election Day; or 
 Have a disability that keeps you from voting at your polling place; or 
 Have a religious belief that prevents you from voting at your polling place on Election Day 
 Deadline to apply for an Absentee ballot  to be mailed  is by 5pm five business days prior to election date  
 Deadline to apply for Absentee ballot and  vote in person  is 12 noon the business day prior to election date 
 
   
 You can fill out an absentee ballot application if: 
 
 You are a U.S. citizen residing overseas; or 
 You are on active military duty; or 
 You are currently incarcerated for a reason other than a felony conviction; or 
 You are requesting an emergency absentee ballot due to hospitalization. 
 
   
 For additional information visit:  http://www.sec.state.ma.us/ele/eleabsentee/absidx.htm 
   
 Voters can also vote by completing and submitting a vote by mail application  
 (click on Voting by Mail link to apply or print an application).    Voting by Mail 
   
 ABSENTEE AND VOTE BY MAIL BALLOTS CAN ALSO BE RETURNED IN PERSON AT THE TOWN CLERK'S OFFICE TUES/WED/THURS 9-4 OR BY PLACING THE SEALED VOTED BALLOT IN THE SECURE  LARGE BLUE DROP BOX  LOCATED TO THE RIGHT OF THE STAIRS OUTSIDE OF THE HENRY WOODS BUILDING LOCATED AT 40 WEST ST.  THE DROP BOX IS AVAILABLE 24/7. 
   
 Testing of voting equipment for the Nov. 3rd State  Election will be conducted  in the Henry Woods Building, 40 West Street- basement- tentatively at 1pm October 21st next to the Town Clerk’s Office.

EARLY VOTED BALLOTS FROM THEIR ENVELOPES  
 In accordance with the provisions of Chapter 54 section 25B as
amended by Section 10 of Chapter 92 of the Acts of 2022, the Town of Barre will
be opening early voted ballots at the Henry Woods Building, located at 40 West
St., 1 st  floor, at the following session:

October 30, 2026             10:00 AM  

 We respectfully ask that observers register in advance (before 5pm
Thursday, October 29 th  ) by emailing  clerk@townofbarre.com   
 A full record of advance removal will be kept for this session.    In accordance with the provisions of Chapter
54 section 25B as amended by Section 10 of Chapter 92 of the Acts of 2022, no
results shall be determined or announced until after the time the polls close
on November 3rd.   At that time, un-official precinct results will be
posted on the outside door of each precinct.  
 Un-official Election Day results will also be posted at the Henry Woods
Building and on the town’s website at  www.townofbarre.com 
. Campaigning on Election Day or Early

 No poster, card, handbill, placard,
picture or circular intended to influence the action of the voter, other than

circulated or distributed in the building where the polling location is
located, on the walls thereof, on the premises located at 584 Main Street,
stand within one hundred and fifty feet (150') of the building entrance door to
